_meta.note: Driven by a scratch stdio driver through Kiro Crew's own PiLaunch, the way test/test_pi_real_adapter.py drives pi: pi-acp 0.0.34 spawning pi 1.4.0 (the Real Adapter lane pin, npm ci in test/real_adapters), the gate extension sealed and read back through the gate launcher (PI_ACP_PI_COMMAND), the per-session MCP handoff, and a scripted OpenAI-compatible model named `scripted` on the loopback interface in pi's own models.json, so no real model or credential was involved; the scratch home was a fresh mode-700 directory, never the user's ~/.kiro/crew. The session is a crewmate WORKER: its session key was recorded as Bot `pixel`'s worker, and the worker spec it ran on is mate_worker.worker_session_spec: a worker base (prompt 'You are the worker.', tools [read], no servers) merged with Bot file `pixel` (tools [@pixel-probe], one stdio MCP server whose one tool, probe_codeword, returns kumquat-17, and a prompt telling the worker to call that tool when asked for the release codeword). The array was not written by hand: AcpClient(acp_backend='pi')'s own resolver (_mirrorless_member_mounts, reading session_mcp_projection by the worker's key) composed ['pixel-probe'], and PiLaunch sealed that into the handoff (['pixel-probe']); the same resolve with no session key composed [] and for a key not recorded as a worker [], neither carrying pixel-probe. The prompt text was the [AGENT SYSTEM PROMPT] block context_assembly.agent_spec._crewmate_worker_prompt built for that worker with pi in ACP_BACKENDS_MATE_WORKER_PROMPT_IN_CONTEXT: the base, the worker principles, then the Bot's sentence, followed by 'What is the release codeword?'. The scripted model calls mcp__pixel_probe__probe_codeword only when the Bot's sentence is in the request it was sent and the tool is in that request's own tool list, then answers with the tool result it got back; both held. The call raised session/request_permission through the gate extension first, the driver answered it through Crew's own build_permission_event under the launch's nonce, and the pixel-probe server logged initialize, notifications/initialized, tools/list, tools/call. The recording host has a working namespace sandbox backend, so the routing's sandbox preflight and the pi read-back and Node probe wraps ran as shipped; the driver spawned the adapter from the launch plan's argv, as test/test_pi_real_adapter.py does; the Bot's crewmate file and the worker's execution record were supplied in-process (mate_file_for_member, read_session_execution, mate_agents_dir), the seams the worker spec reads; every other step ran as shipped. Reductions: no configOptions select was cut (the scratch catalog offers one model); 1 available_commands_update frame(s) dropped: it carries the recording host's own command inventory; the session id is replaced with the synthetic pi-session-1; the working directory with <cwd>; the confirm dialogs' uuids with synthetic pi-ui-perm-N ids.
